derived.label: body force per unit mass g
derived.note: = 1.2e-5 × strength 1. Reading k as a Darcy permeability needs creeping flow, which holds while the pore Reynolds number stays below one; coarse grains and a strong drive can leave that regime, and the run reports the value it reached

derived.label: time steps
derived.note: k is reported as 'transient' unless the last 10 % of the run changed it by < 1 %

plots.title: Permeability (Darcy)
plots.explain: k = ν U_D / g from the final frame: ν = (τ − ½)/3, U_D the superficial velocity (flow averaged over the whole sample including solid cells) and g the body force per unit mass (Guo forcing; here g = 1.2e-05). A pore-average velocity ⟨u⟩_fluid = U_D/φ is reported separately (0.00343666). One point next to an empirical curve does not establish agreement: the Kozeny–Carman line is for 3-D packed beds and is drawn for orientation. To check Darcy behaviour, sweep the porosity or the seed (same φ, different connectivity) with the sweep tool; the run reports k from the final state and should be run long enough for the readout to have settled (increase Duration and compare).
